items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED: What does the `any-owner-non-exclusive` joint-owner consent rule actually authorize?

WHY IT MATTERS: It is one of exactly three consent rules recordable on every master, and it is the only one that lets a single co-owner act WITHOUT the others. It decides whether one member of a band can license the group's master alone. It is named in three places and defined in none.

WHY IT CANNOT BE INFERRED: The obvious answer — the US default, where co-owners may grant non-exclusive licences unilaterally subject to a duty to account — is exactly the jurisdictional default 09.01.03 D-04 and DT-10 forbid the platform from adopting on the parties' behalf ('The platform does not pick a jurisdiction's default'). Your ratified D-43/CQ-06 decision specified the `majority-by-share` predicate in full and is silent on this one, so this is not a stale value awaiting a sweep; it is a rule that was named and never written.

FOUR SUB-CALLS, each a real product decision:
(a) WHICH ACTIONS does it reach? Non-exclusive master licence only (the name suggests this), or also release/distribute and derivative creation? Five Control Summary actions are gated on the consent evaluator.
(b) DUTY TO ACCOUNT: does the unilaterally-acting owner owe the others their share of what they collected? And if so, does WeJammin compute and enforce that split, or merely record the obligation? Enforcing it makes the platform a participant; recording it only makes the rule commercially hollow.
(c) NOTIFICATION: are the other owners told at grant time, and may they object? Silent unilateral licensing of a co-owned master is the fact pattern that generates the disputes this domain exists to prevent.
(d) CONTROL SUMMARY RENDERING: what do the five consent-gated action rows show when this is the recorded rule? `No recorded obstacle` would be wrong (it is a positive authorization, not an absence), but the feature has exactly three verdicts (D-05) and none of them fits. This may force a fourth verdict, which is a change to the domain's most load-bearing display contract.

RECOMMENDATION: Answer (a) narrowly — non-exclusive master licence only — and (c) yes, notify at grant. Those two together make the rule mean something specific and keep it inside the existing three-verdict model. (b) is the genuinely expensive one and can be deferred to /create-prd-architecture once (a) is fixed. If you would rather not spend the decision at all, the cheapest safe option is to REMOVE the third rule from v1 entirely and ship two (`unanimous`, `majority-by-share`) — nothing downstream depends on it, and an unspecified rule on a live master is worse than an absent one.

items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED: Is a bought-out (work-for-hire) contributor a 0% row inside the ownership ledger, or structurally absent from it?

THE CONFLICT: Two files that each own their side say opposite things, and both are reasoned.
- 09.01.02 (owns the ledger and its invariants): INV-6 'Zero rows are rows — a 0% party (work-for-hire contributor, non-featured performer) is a valid row and is not pruned. Absence and zero are different statements.' Its edge case renders the row as '0% — paid by fee, not by share', linked to the WFH designation. Its cross-cut note says plainly: 'WFH is why INV-6 exists.'
- 09.02.03 (owns the designation): 'Records the party's ABSENCE FROM the ownership ledger... They are not a 0% row by accident; they are absent by agreement.' Its DT-01 says a bare 0% row cannot distinguish '0% by agreement' from '0% because nobody said', and resolves: 'present in the view, structurally distinct in the record.'
- 09.02.01 D-09 then DEPENDS on absence: 'A bought-out drummer is not a ledger party and is consenting to a fee, not a share; showing them commercially sensitive percentages protects nobody and leaks to everybody.'

WHY IT IS NOT A TIDINESS QUESTION: 09.01.02 D-01 requires every named party to see every row and every value before consenting, and D-07 grants read on the whole ledger to anyone named on it. If the WFH contributor is a row, those two decisions hand every session player who was ever bought out a full view of the writers' and owners' percentages — which is precisely what D-09 exists to prevent. If they are absent, then INV-6's stated reason for existing is wrong and needs rewriting.

TWO COHERENT RESOLUTIONS:
(A) THEY ARE A ROW, and D-07's read-grant is narrowed to CONSENTING ledger parties. A WFH contributor consents to the designation, not to the ledger, so the whole-ledger visibility obligation never fires for them. Keeps INV-6 and its 'absence and zero are different statements' principle intact — which is a genuinely valuable property, because it is how the registry tells a completed deal from an abandoned sheet. Cost: D-07 must be rewritten, and 'named on the ledger but cannot read it' is a new and slightly awkward category.
(B) THEY ARE ABSENT, and INV-6 is rescoped to non-featured performers only. Keeps D-09 and 09.02.01 Q-06 exactly as drafted. Cost: 09.01.02's INV-6, its edge case and its cross-cut note all need rewriting, and the 'agreement vs absence' distinction has to be carried entirely by the designation record rather than by the ledger — which is what 09.02.03 DT-01 already proposes ('structurally distinct in the record').

RECOMMENDATION: (B). It is the reading 09.02.01 Q-06 already assumes, it needs no change to the consent/visibility model (the riskiest thing to touch), and 09.02.03 DT-01's 'present in the view, structurally distinct in the record' already delivers the visibility that INV-6 was reaching for — the contributor appears in the capture view via their designation and their performer/credit record, without acquiring ledger read. Under (B) the fix is confined to three restatements in 09.01.02. Please answer this together with 09.02.01 Q-06; they are one call.

items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED: When a 14-player ensemble (orchestra, choir, horn section) is engaged through one contractor, does the buyout close on the contractor's single consent, or does it require all 14 players' individual consents?

THE CONFLICT: Both files ratified a decision about this exact scenario, and they are incompatible.
- 09.02.01 D-12 (resolving its Q-03): 'one fee designation consented by the contractor, who attests they hold the engagement and the authority to bind it — the platform records the attestation and asserts nothing about it. Consent load: 3 ledger parties + 1 contractor, not 14.' The players get non-blocking performer rows and credits. Producer sees 'Horn section (4) — engaged via {contractor}, fee'.
- 09.02.03 D-16: 'Bulk propose, never bulk consent. One tap standing in for N extinguishments is manufactured consent — the evidentiary garbage the domain exists to replace.' Its edge case: 'The platform can bulk-propose (one term-set, one action, 14 notifications) but cannot bulk-consent: the extinguishment is individual.' User sees 'Buyout proposed to 14 players — waiting on 11.'

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT STAKE: whether the most common professional session on the platform closes in the room or blocks for days. D-12 is right that a fixer signing for an orchestra is genuine, universal industry practice. D-16 is right that a consent record the signer did not personally give is exactly the evidentiary weakness this whole domain was built to eliminate — and that weakness would sit on WeJammin's most impressive-looking records.

THE ONLY CLEAN WAY THROUGH is to decide what the contractor's single consent legally covers:
(A) AGENCY IS MODELLED. Domain 01 models the contractor→player agency relationship as recorded authority, and the contractor's consent genuinely binds the players because they authorised it in advance. Consent load 4. This is the only option that makes D-12 true without violating D-16, because the consents are not manufactured — they are delegated. Cost: real work in domain 01, and 09.02.03 Q-06 is already routed to /create-prd-security for exactly this.
(B) NO AGENCY; ATTESTATION ONLY. The contractor attests authority, the platform records the attestation and asserts nothing (which is what D-12 literally says today). Consent load 4, but the resulting record is an assertion by one person about 14 people's rights — which is what D-16 calls evidentiary garbage. Fast, and it quietly weakens the asset.
(C) 14 INDIVIDUAL CONSENTS. D-16 holds strictly. Evidentially perfect, and it means an orchestral date cannot close until 14 people tap a link, which will not happen on the day and may never happen.

RECOMMENDATION: (A), and accept that it blocks on domain 01. It is the only option that keeps both ratified decisions true, and agency is a real legal relationship rather than a platform invention — recording it is squarely inside 'hold facts, route judgements' (domain D-04). Interim posture while 01 is built: use (C) for the extinguishment but let the session close on the fee designation, so the money and the credits are right even where the buyout is still pending. Whatever you choose, 09.02.01 Q-03 must be REOPENED — it is currently marked RESOLVED on the strength of D-12, and 09.02.03 Q-06's framing ('only whether agency is modelled') understates the disagreement.

The chain carries `platform-witnessed`/`evidence-attached`/`asserted` on each EVENT (09.03.01 D-01, the fact layer); the record-level `captured`/`asserted`/`imported` provenance class is the DERIVED badge the lookup renders. Residual tracked as 09.06.04 Q-05: the derivation is genuinely underspecified at two edges — `evidence-attached` has no counterpart class (does a paper-contract transfer render `captured` or `asserted`?), and `imported` has no counterpart event level (the chain would record a feed ingest as `asserted`, losing the 'nobody attested' distinction CX-07 depends on for WeJammin's own bulk data). items.ownerBrief:
DECISION NEEDED: Who may take down a co-owned master — any single owner, a majority by share, or whatever the recorded consent rule says?

WHY IT HAS NO ANSWER YET: 12.05.01 DT-03 marked 'the artist can always take down their own release' as CONTESTED and routed the call to domains 01/09; domain 09 then declared it 'unresolved' inline and opened no question. So the rule domain 12 inherits was never written, and 12.05.01 cannot be specified until it is.

WHY IT DOES NOT FALL OUT OF THE CONSENT RULE YOU ALREADY RATIFIED: D-07 governs grants, sale, encumbrance creation and derivatives — affirmative acts that DISPOSE of the right. A takedown is a WITHDRAWAL, and the asymmetry is real:
- Require unanimity (or majority) to withdraw, and you trap a co-owner in a release they want gone. The cases that matter are not hypothetical: a track someone is being harassed over, or one released against their wishes in the first place.
- Permit any owner to withdraw unilaterally, and one member can delete the band's catalogue — and unlike a bad licence, a takedown destroys chart position, playlist placement and algorithmic standing that do not come back when the record returns.
Neither outcome is derivable from anything recorded. It is a values trade about which failure you prefer, which is why it is yours.

OPTIONS:
(A) ANY OWNER MAY WITHDRAW, unilaterally, recorded as a chain event and notified to the others. Protects the trapped co-owner, the party with the most acute harm. Exposes the catalogue to one angry member.
(B) THE RECORDED CONSENT RULE GOVERNS, same as any other master action. Consistent and easy to explain; means a harassed artist cannot remove their own record without their co-owners' agreement.
(C) SPLIT BY MOTIVE: any owner may withdraw unilaterally on a declared personal-harm ground (recorded, attested, notified); everything else follows the recorded consent rule. Serves both cases at the cost of asking the platform to hold a category it must not adjudicate — though note it would only RECORD the declared ground, never evaluate it, which stays inside domain D-04.

RECOMMENDATION: (C), with the declared ground recorded and never assessed. (A) hands one member a catalogue-deletion button; (B) tells someone being harassed over a record that they need their bandmates' permission to stop it. (C) costs one extra field and one attestation, and it is the same shape as the override mechanism 09.01.03 D-06 already uses — attested reason, chain event, notification to the affected parties. Please answer this together with 12.05.01 Q-01; they are one call, and 12.05.01 is blocked on it.
